text:
maria: Heads up — found a confusing auth/slot bug: `rw upload` can attempt uploads to the wrong project when env vars, CLI flags, and key scopes disagree. Repro below.

devon: paste the log?

maria: short repro: 
```
$ REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme-prod rw upload --file weights.bin
Using project: acme-prod (inferred from REDWOOD_PROJECT)
Uploading chunk 1/10...
Error: 403 Forbidden: API key not authorized for project acme-prod
```

kevin: is the key project-scoped or org-scoped?

maria: key is org-scoped but its profile default project is `acme-staging`. I expected the CLI to either respect the env OR validate and fail before starting the upload. Instead it streams a few chunks and then 403s.

devon: ack. Current precedence is weird: CLI flag > env (REDWOOD_PROJECT) > key profile default > key-embedded scope. That means a dev with REDWOOD_PROJECT set can accidentally point at prod while using a key that only allows staging.

kevin: proposal: 1) compute effective project as: explicit `--project` flag > REDWOOD_PROJECT env > key default project. 2) perform a preflight scope-check before sending payloads: if key lacks permission, surface a clear error: "API key not permitted for project X (key allows: Y)" and exit. No partial uploads.

maria: yes please. Also add a non-interactive CI-friendly check: `rw auth info --ci` returns nonzero if scopes mismatch so CI can fail early.

sam: interactive fallback idea: if key is org-scoped and env project not allowed, prompt: "Use key default project acme-staging instead? [y/N]" but respect `--no-prompt` for CI.

auth-bot: created issue RBW-4890 (labels: devex, cli, auth, p2)

devon: i'll open a tiny PR to add the preflight check + better error message and a `rw auth info --ci` flag. @eng-runtime can we also add an optional response header `X-Allowed-Projects: acme-staging,acme-test` when returning 403 so clients can present helpful guidance?

kevin: one more ask: docs/onboarding should explicitly document precedence and show recommended patterns for CI and services (use `rw auth info --ci` in build step; prefer key with explicit project scope for prod pipelines).

maria: thanks all — this should stop a few scary accidental uploads. :thumbsup:
